title: A new atlas of Mississauga
summary: A 56-page atlas and a matched Downtown aerial bring the city’s changing neighbourhoods into print.

details.heading: A view across Square One
details.text: I re-rendered the city views and aligned all three skyline stages to one camera. The new edition includes 11 building booklets, a sharper atlas reader and 30 detailed building profiles with photographs and map links.

records.heading: Three ways to see Downtown
paragraphs: Switch between existing buildings, construction and proposals from the same point above Square One.
records.caption: Downtown construction near Square One. Model by Daniel Sultan.

records.heading: Explore 20 neighbourhoods
paragraphs: Open a neighbourhood for its aerial view, buildings and atlas page.

records.heading: How to read the M City models
paragraphs: M1, M2 and M5 have individual exterior studies. The future phases show dated proposals. Each model links to its sources.

title: How I modelled the M City towers
summary: A developer’s question gave me a chance to explain how I built the tower studies.

details.heading: The modelling process
details.text: I combined municipal 3D data, planning drawings, floor plans and photographs, then refined the geometry in Python and Blender. The published M1, M2 and M5 models let readers inspect the result from any side.

illustration.caption: M City M1 and M2 in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Five neighbourhoods in new pictures
summary: New image releases covered East Credit and Creditview, Meadowvale Village, Lorne Park, Churchill Meadows and Lisgar.

details.heading: From model to gallery
details.text: I released landscape and portrait images of the neighbourhoods. Merner Row Design also confirmed the public design credit for the house studies. Thanks to the studio for helping me read roof details that were hard to see from the street.

illustration.caption: Lorne Park with proposed buildings in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Easier browsing on small screens
summary: Controls and spacing across the map and gallery were updated for smaller screens.

details.heading: A roof detail from the designer
details.text: On the same day, Merner Row Design explained the low gable joining the old house and the addition at 41 Bay Street. It runs across the two main roof ridges. The explanation gave me a clearer reference for the exterior.

title: Revising the front of 41 Bay Street
summary: I centred the upper windows and removed a short section of veranda railing.

details.heading: Checking the next detail
details.text: After adjusting the windows and railing, I sent my model changes back to Merner Row Design. I asked how the small roof connected the original house and its addition.

illustration.caption: The front of 41 Bay Street in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: A closer look at the windows on Bay Street
summary: Designer feedback pinpointed the upper windows in the 41 Bay Street study.

details.heading: A second set of eyes
details.text: I sent my revised house studies to Merner Row Design. The designer marked the windows on the front of 41 Bay Street, giving me a specific correction to make in the next model.

title: Downtown in three stages
summary: See the existing skyline, buildings under construction and a possible future from the same viewpoint.

details.heading: Following the changes
details.text: I prepared wide views of Downtown for all three stages and organised the skyline film around the same sequence. The updated atlas put the views together for print.

records.heading: New Downtown views
paragraphs: The Downtown gallery now has revised wide views and skyline views of existing buildings, dated construction and the future scenario. The skyline film and Downtown pages in the 35-page picture atlas have also been updated.
records.caption: Downtown with proposed buildings in the November 9 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: A new gallery for city views
summary: Citywide pictures and neighbourhood renders came together in one gallery.

details.heading: Finding a particular view
details.text: I connected the gallery and map viewer so a neighbourhood could be explored from its pictures. Newly reviewed model details and full-size city renders accompanied the release.

title: A closer look at M City
summary: New views show the shapes, glazing and façades of the M City towers in Downtown.

details.heading: The skyline in context
details.text: I revised tower forms and glazing for the M1–M5 studies and refreshed the city views. A separate study of 50 High Street East used the project drawings to interpret the façade frames and roof arches.

records.heading: A closer look at M City
paragraphs: M1–M5 have revised tower forms, glazing and facade detail. The new views place these approximate studies within the surrounding city.
records.caption: M City in the Downtown model. Model by Daniel Sultan.

records.heading: A fresh view of the whole city
paragraphs: The picture atlas collects city and neighbourhood views in one PDF.
records.caption: Citywide model with proposed developments. Model by Daniel Sultan.

records.heading: 50 High Street East
paragraphs: An approximate study of the planned building adds facade frames, roof arches and glazing from December 2025 drawings.

records.heading: M6–M8 plans under review
paragraphs: Urban Capital is reviewing plans and tenure after the October 23 sale to UC M City Inc. It says Rogers retains no ownership, financing or development role in those lands. No condo launch is imminent.

On October 29, the City confirmed it had received no revised plans and issued no building permits. The last submissions show M6 at 58 storeys and 889 homes and M7/M8 at 51 and 46 storeys, with 1,457 homes combined.

records.heading: Browsing and downloads
paragraphs: Images and PDFs open in-page with separate downloads. The Downloads page collects the atlas, prints and skyline film. The Subway concept has been retired.

links.label: See M City M1 and M2

title: Checking plans for M City’s final phases
summary: I asked the City what records it held for M6, M7 and M8 after the land sale.

details.heading: What a drawing can tell us
details.text: City planning staff sent drawings for comparison. They helped distinguish what had been drawn from what could be confirmed about the future phases. The site continues to distinguish the proposed skyline from the buildings that are already there.

links.label: See the City’s M City project

illustration.caption: The proposed Downtown skyline in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Fairview, Superior and Maritz Drive
summary: Fairview gained more surrounding homes. Two industrial buildings gained closer exterior studies.

details.heading: Material details at Maritz
details.text: SG&M Architects Inc. supplied a photograph and material information for 6710 Maritz Drive. I used those references to check the front elevation and publish comparison views. Thanks to SG&M Architects Inc. for the design references.

records.heading: More of Fairview in the map
paragraphs: Existing homes around Fairview have been added to the Citywide model, giving the neighbourhood more of its surrounding context.
records.caption: Fairview, as shown in the October study. City of Mississauga · Ontario data · © OpenStreetMap.

records.heading: A closer look at 275 Superior
paragraphs: An approximate facade study adds glazing, cladding and the entrance canopy. It now opens directly in the Citywide map.
Photo reference: David Lasker/Cityscape Photography.
records.caption: Façade study by Daniel Sultan. Photo reference by David Lasker / Cityscape Photography.

records.heading: A new Citywide view
paragraphs: The Citywide image and atlas cover show the reviewed city assembly against a pale-blue background. The atlas’s district pages keep their earlier edition.
Building studies now open images and PDFs in-page. The Citywide map also loads the reviewed 275 Superior study directly, with added context around Fairview. Coverage still varies by area.

title: Oro joins the Downtown model
summary: The tower study could now be viewed in its surrounding city blocks.

details.heading: Putting Oro in place
details.text: I integrated the source-based study with the city scene and kept its qualifications with the model. The same release improved the delivery of large model files.

illustration.caption: Oro at Edge Towers in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Opening a building in its surroundings
summary: Detailed studies became easier to reach directly in the city map.

details.heading: From the catalogue to the map
details.text: I connected individual model views with their positions in the wider scene. Visitors could open the building they had chosen without having to find it again in the map.

title: Edge and Avia, tower by tower
summary: The individual towers gained their own detailed previews.

details.heading: Four buildings, up close
details.text: I added Edge and Avia previews with a lighter viewer for phones. SG&M Architects Inc. also shared exterior references for 6710 Maritz Drive and identified the precast concrete and grey glazing that would guide that separate façade study.

illustration.caption: Avia 1 in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: East Credit and Creditview on the map
summary: A detailed neighbourhood scene brought more of the area into the interactive map.

details.heading: Views you can explore
details.text: I added the East Credit and Creditview coverage and revised how the gallery labels its neighbourhood pictures. Building studies also gained document previews, so a reader could look inside a PDF before downloading it.

records.heading: A clearer view of the city
paragraphs: The 3D map opens closer to each neighbourhood, with neutral daylight and drag-to-move controls. Zoom keeps the same viewing direction, ordinary area changes preserve the angle, and the compass returns the view to north.
Turn on Surrounding city to load nearby existing buildings and a wider city backdrop. Detail varies with the available models. The selected study is not an official neighbourhood boundary.

Reframed gallery views keep the square edges of the source studies outside the picture. The white footer has more balanced spacing, and the images to share use a clearer page layout. On-site image bars are clean; source notes sit beside the images, with a short source line on downloads where needed.

records.heading: A closer view of East Credit and Creditview
paragraphs: East Credit and Creditview now have a closer 3D view, with streets, trees and transit connections. The map covers 20 areas, including the city overview.

illustration.caption: East Credit and Creditview in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Meadowvale Village in detail
summary: A new neighbourhood view arrived alongside house and podium corrections elsewhere in the city.

details.heading: What changed
details.text: I added Meadowvale Village, repaired stretched house surfaces in Erin Mills and Erindale, and restored the construction podium below Exchange in Downtown. Picture credits, a status key and a camera-correct north arrow made the new views easier to read.

records.heading: Picture credits and status key
paragraphs: The October 22 image update added clearer status keys and creator credits. Earlier images keep their original dates.

records.heading: A closer view of Meadowvale Village
paragraphs: The October 22 update added a closer view of Meadowvale Village, with more City-source buildings and mapped surroundings.

records.heading: The missing base below Exchange
paragraphs: The construction view had a missing section beneath EX2. I restored the shared base from the original model and fitted its lower edge to the map ground. The towers keep their original positions and shapes.
The small ground fit is approximate. This is a dated construction illustration; the model’s finished surfaces do not show the exact state of work on site.

records.heading: A neighbourhood model correction
paragraphs: I removed a stretched source-model surface in Erin Mills and Erindale and closed the affected house side using its existing outline. That small closure is approximate. Nearby houses also return to their usual pale colour.
Other buildings and transit routes are unchanged. The gallery pictures are being reviewed separately.

illustration.caption: Meadowvale Village in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: A closer view of Lisgar and Argentia
summary: The model gained a detailed view of the neighbourhood and clearer shading on buildings.

details.heading: A wider local scene
details.text: I expanded the context around Lisgar and Argentia so buildings could be read alongside the streets nearby. The same release refined how light falls across the buildings.

records.heading: Clearer buildings and a wider map
paragraphs: Coloured towers now show their separate sides and sharper corners. The usual navigation stays the same.

Lisgar & Argentia adds a detailed view of retained City buildings and mapped surroundings. It reaches 2,921 additional existing source parts. This measures map coverage and does not count newly verified buildings.

illustration.caption: Lisgar and Argentia in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Checking the Port Credit bridge record
summary: I added the City’s procurement record to the bridge study and corrected the tender note.

details.heading: What the record establishes
details.text: I checked the City’s tender and its award record. The public material helped document the project but did not supply the engineering drawings needed to verify the detailed bridge shape.

title: Following your place on the homepage
summary: The homepage began highlighting its sections as readers scrolled.

details.heading: Knowing where you are
details.text: I linked the section highlight to the part of the page in view and simplified the navigation around it. That made it easier to move through a long homepage.

title: A second angle on Boundless Flight
summary: The artist’s photograph helped me see the mural around a corner that the first views missed.

details.heading: Around the container
details.text: When I modelled the artwork, I had to follow the painted design across the sides of a shipping container. A second angle clarified the short side. Thanks to Wandy Cheng, the artist behind Boundless Flight.

title: Sherobee Road and Churchill Meadows
summary: Shared exterior references improved the Sherobee study. Churchill Meadows gained a wider scene.

details.heading: From reference to street
details.text: I compared the old and revised Sherobee exteriors and placed the Winding Trail and 228 Queen Street South studies in their city surroundings. The update also added a detailed Churchill Meadows view.

records.heading: Churchill Meadows and two building studies
paragraphs: Churchill Meadows now has its own detailed view. The Winding Trail and 228 Queen Street South studies also appear in their surroundings, with some ground details still approximate.

records.heading: New reference renders
paragraphs: Shared references helped me improve Winding Trail, Paisley, Sherobee, museum buildings, Leslie Log House and 228 Queen Street South, and make new studies of Port Credit Lighthouse and part of Conference at the Council House. The new page shows matched views of earlier and updated models, alongside the details I still need to check.

The earlier October 17 release added these standalone render studies. This later update places Winding Trail and 228 Queen Street South in the city map and adds the Churchill Meadows view. The existing gallery pictures and downloadable atlas have not been regenerated.

illustration.caption: 2200 Sherobee Road in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Checking the South Common exterior
summary: The timber supplier reviewed my exterior study of the community centre and library.

details.heading: What the references showed
details.text: I contacted Element5 about its work on South Common. Its site plan and construction photographs helped me interpret the finished exterior. Element5 supplied the cross-laminated timber for the project.

title: Reading the shelter drawings at Fairwinds Park
summary: New references showed how the shade structure’s roof meets its four posts.

details.heading: From drawing to model
details.text: ABC Recreation supplied drawings and views for the shelter. I used the dimensions to build an initial study of the roof slope and post layout, and later checked its colours. Design and reference credit goes to ABC Recreation and Poligon.

illustration.alt: The boat-shaped shelter in Fairwinds Park
illustration.caption: The boat-shaped shelter in Fairwinds Park in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

share.alt: The boat-shaped shelter in Fairwinds Park

title: Filling a gap on the Clarkson waterfront
summary: The land and buildings around Harding Estate now read together in the Clarkson view.

details.heading: Where land meets water
details.text: I filled in the missing mainland context around the estate. The water shown along the waterfront was also bounded to the area covered by each city model.

illustration.caption: Clarkson waterfront in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: A clearer way into the 3D map
summary: The map and site navigation gained clearer labels, and the header stayed visible while scrolling.

details.heading: Moving around the site
details.text: I shortened navigation labels and made the header slimmer. Merner Row Design also sent annotated sketches for the Port Credit house studies, useful for checking the next round of exterior models.

title: What the latest plans actually showed
summary: I checked the planning records behind projects in Erin Mills, Lakeview, Port Credit and other neighbourhoods.

details.heading: Reading a city decision
details.text: I distinguished a site-plan approval from a construction start at Pier House. At Erin Mills Town Centre, I documented the conditional Tribunal decision and the work that still stood between that decision and construction.

records.heading: The latest checks
paragraphs: New planning and construction evidence is now recorded, alongside the sites that still need reliable architecture. A locator marks a researched project; it does not stand in for a finished building model.

records.heading: Erin Mills Town Centre — northwest phase
paragraphs: The Tribunal approved the nine-tower, 3,162-home settlement in principle on September 24, 2026. The illustrated 20–37-storey layout is already incorporated. The Final Order remains conditional, and holding requirements, subdivision and individual site plans still matter. The settlement adds at least 2,047 m² of non-residential space and a 4,206 m² park.
Existing geometry retained; status/timeline correction only

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: Living Arts Centre precinct vision
paragraphs: The City is studying a vision for 12 acres around the Living Arts Centre and Community Common. Public engagement and business-case work are planned for fall 2026 to winter 2027, with recommendations to Council in spring 2027. The Living Arts Centre remains open.
Existing geometry retained; status/timeline correction only

records.heading: 6020 Winston Churchill Boulevard
paragraphs: The four-storey, 22-home building has site-plan approval and an issued new-building permit. September reporting and Peel identify construction underway. The full model is a planned envelope; its current structural stage has not been measured.
The illustration shows the planned building envelope. It does not establish a measured construction stage.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: Pier House
paragraphs: The Block 4 plan depicts 164 townhomes in 19 rows. The City’s Section 47 site-plan record now gives September 17, 2026 approval. Construction has not been independently verified.
The model retains the 19 townhouse rows from the plan. Site-plan approval does not establish a construction start.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: Lakeview DXE Club
paragraphs: Two mid-rise buildings of eight and twelve storeys continued under a receiver. PCL reported the 397-unit development topped off in July 2026.
The model retains the documented eight- and twelve-storey buildings. The City GIS record lists 478 units, while PCL reports 397; that difference remains noted.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: 2935–2955 Mississauga Road
paragraphs: The April 2026 resubmission proposes a 12-storey apartment with 196 homes and 15 stacked townhouses, 211 homes total. The City webpage still says 20 townhouses, but current architecture and servicing agree on 15. Four existing City source components already represent the site.
Existing City buildings are already shown. Current roof and terrace details remain to be compared with the newer plans.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: 2184–2194 Oneida Crescent
paragraphs: A June 2026 application proposes eight detached homes in total, including the retained house at 2184 Oneida. Four freehold lots and a four-home common-element condominium are shown; seven homes would be new.
Site marked; the plans show seven new houses and one retained house. Their roof designs and actual heights are not yet verified.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: 7 Elmwood Avenue North · supportive housing
paragraphs: FSIG Elmwood GP Inc. and Indwell plan 25 supportive homes in Port Credit. The City records an active site-plan application, and Peel still identifies the project as planning. The programme’s forecast construction dates do not confirm that work has started.
Site marked; the new building needs a reliable current site plan and elevations before its shape is added.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: 1407 Lakeshore Road East
paragraphs: Anthem’s current application is for 85 apartments and ground-floor retail. Earlier records describe 83 apartments over nine storeys and a separate 96-townhome scheme.
The map marks the site. Its building shape awaits current plans and elevations.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: Creekside Apartments
paragraphs: Indwell’s four-storey Creekside project at 1639 Lakeshore Road West is under construction. The City permit and current Peel project page identify 51 homes. Indwell’s earlier page lists 50 homes and a 2026 opening, while Peel’s current forecast is Q4 2027.
Site marked; the new building needs a reliable current site plan and elevations before its shape is added.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: 1110 Lorne Park Road · six townhomes
paragraphs: The City records an approved six-townhome scheme and later removal of its holding symbol. This older project’s site has now been marked on the map. A construction start in October 2026 has not been verified. Current delivery and exact architecture remain unconfirmed.
Site marked; the new building needs a reliable current site plan and elevations before its shape is added.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: Port Credit Active Transportation Bridge
paragraphs: A walking and cycling connection from Front Street North to Port Credit Memorial Park. The City still labels it in progress and documents the girder launch. No public opening confirmation was recovered.
The City tender confirms a 66 m clear span. Final drawings are still needed for the deck height, width, abutment positions and alignment before the bridge is modelled.

links.label: See the site and model record

records.heading: New reference-based building views
paragraphs: Shared references helped improve NRC, the UTM Meeting Place canopy, Bell Gairdner Estate, the Buddhist temple and Fairwinds Park.

links.label: See the new models and original renders

title: Turning Aldo Drive towards its driveway
summary: I corrected the house’s orientation and checked new planning evidence around the city.

details.heading: The front of the house
details.text: The previous view did not face the driveway correctly. I turned the study into position and refreshed the comparisons. That day I also updated the zoning and demolition evidence for 50 High Street East.

records.heading: 2155 Leanne Boulevard
paragraphs: Added the revised ten-storey apartment and eight townhouse blocks: 383 homes in all. The model follows the current plan, with smaller roof details and ground levels clearly qualified.

records.heading: 50–60 Harborn Road
paragraphs: Added the twelve proposed townhomes in two mansard-roof rows. These are a received proposal, with approval and construction still unconfirmed.

records.heading: 1970–1980 Fowler Drive
paragraphs: July plans add a 24-storey tower beside the two existing buildings. The model distinguishes the roof levels and simplifies the balconies and finishes.
The official-plan amendment took effect on 29 October 2026. The City’s 10 November register lists the zoning amendment as in force. Construction permission and timing remain unverified.

records.heading: 6344 Ninth Line
paragraphs: The three six-storey buildings moved about 409 m to the correct parcel, beside homes shown in City data. The model uses the posted roof levels. Proposed grades are approximate, and published plans give different counts of 141 and 153 homes.

records.heading: 1225 Dundas Street East
paragraphs: Replaced the old 18-storey version with the current stepped 16-storey design, open courtyard and townhomes. The source roof height is 51.94 m; the new zoning maximum is 52 m.

records.heading: 42–46 Park / Park and Elizabeth
paragraphs: The building body measures 95 m in the reference plans. The newer rooftop allowance brings the maximum to 106.5 m. The model approximates the roof shape and placement. Demolition was reported at the site.

records.heading: Byngmount Shores
paragraphs: Corrected Byngmount Shores to the primary-confirmed seven-storey form and 150 affordable rentals. Its 27.5 m reference height still needs a current dimensioned elevation. October photographs show unfinished construction.

records.heading: 60 Dundas Street East
paragraphs: Added the missing site as a zoning-envelope study. Its permitted 16-, 32- and 31-storey zones are shown in violet; current architectural floor plates are still being checked.

records.heading: 49 South Service Road
paragraphs: Added the controlling 29-storey, 95 m Tribunal permission as a permitted-height study. Its outline and ground placement are approximate, and the site-plan process is still active.

records.heading: Village Green
paragraphs: Added the three-building rental project. Current permits confirm 431 homes and eight, eight and nine storeys. The reference form is violet because metre heights and detailed current elevations remain unverified.

records.heading: 44–45 Longview Place
paragraphs: Added the three proposed house footprints and pitched-roof references. The current plans and older elevations disagree slightly on heights and split-level storey counts, so the violet model keeps those limits visible.

records.heading: Above Condos / 30 Bristol Road East
paragraphs: Added a named Above Condos record and linked public references. The two towers and shared podium were already in the City geometry, so no duplicate building was added.

records.heading: New planning decisions
paragraphs: The October 8 notices record September 29 passage for 2155 Leanne Boulevard, 1970–1980 Fowler Drive, 1225 Dundas East, 6344 Ninth Line, 3115 Hurontario, 44–45 Longview Place. The notices listed October 28 as the appeal deadline. Later decisions are recorded in the individual project records. Some sites also retain holding conditions. Council passage does not establish construction permission or the start of work.

Birch’s site-plan approval is now recorded separately from its unverified construction status. A City-owned Kariya parkland parcel has also been designated as public open space; that change does not alter the proposed Exchange condo towers.

illustration.caption: The driveway side of 1422 Aldo Drive in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: Correcting the roof at 1422 Aldo Drive
summary: A contributor spotted a roof shape that needed to change in the exterior study.

details.heading: What I corrected
details.text: I revised the house to show the flat roof and released new views so the change could be checked against the earlier model.

illustration.caption: The roof at 1422 Aldo Drive in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

title: First exterior studies for Bay, Peter and John
summary: I sent the three house studies back to the designer for a closer look.

details.heading: From drawings to model
details.text: I used drawings and photographs to make approximate models of the three Port Credit houses, then sent the views to Merner Row Design for review. The roof shapes and porch details needed a designer’s eye.

illustration.alt: The front of 42 Peter Street South
illustration.caption: The front of 42 Peter Street South in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

share.alt: The front of 42 Peter Street South

title: References for three Port Credit homes
summary: Merner Row Design responded to my request for exterior references.

details.heading: Starting the studies
details.text: I had asked about 42 Peter Street South. The exchange led to studies of that house, 41 Bay Street and 42 John Street South. The three houses have different additions, rooflines and porches.

illustration.alt: The front of 42 John Street South
illustration.caption: The front of 42 John Street South in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

share.alt: The front of 42 John Street South

title: Checking a historical design before placing it
summary: A source model and the building visible on the site told different stories.

details.heading: A model with limits
details.text: Historical mapping helped identify the property, but newer exterior references differed from the supplied design. I kept the current building in the map and documented why the older design remained a research reference.

title: Updating projects that had changed direction
summary: Project-team and municipal records helped me retire two outdated proposals.

details.heading: Following two design changes
details.text: I removed the old warehouse proposal at 7055 Tranmere Drive and distinguished the earlier condominium scheme at 6620 Rothschild Trail from a newer townhouse application for the same land.

title: Two missing Block Nine towers
summary: A gap in the Downtown model led me back to the City’s building footprints and residential directory.

details.heading: Rebuilding the pair
details.text: I placed the completed North and South towers at 4085 and 4055 Parkside Village Drive, including their connected podium. The City lists 25 and 34 storeys. I used the developer’s brochure to interpret their positions on the shared base.

title: Sharing the Streetsville view
summary: I sent the skyline panorama and a short film to a local councillor’s office.

details.heading: Showing the project
details.text: I had first raised the idea of a city model earlier in the year. This time I could share the working website and the visuals and invite feedback on Streetsville and Meadowvale.

title: 905HUB features Future Mississauga
summary: 905HUB shared the project with local readers.

details.heading: The feature
details.text: The post introduced the city model to people following Mississauga’s changing skyline. The original feature is still available on 905HUB’s Instagram.

title: Cooksville and Clarkson from the design models
summary: Source models brought the proposed towers and podiums at both GO stations into clearer focus.

details.heading: From the design files
details.text: I used Arup’s seven-tower Cooksville design and Zeidler’s seven-tower Clarkson massing to rebuild the two station areas. For South Banks, I used exterior references to revise the cross-gabled roofs on nine blocks.

title: Keeping the Lakeview pier visible
summary: A waterfront update preserved the pier while I compared two possible City Centre transit corridors.

details.heading: An earlier transit study
details.text: The routes were alternatives in a design study. I kept the Lakeview pier visible alongside the waterfront context. The present-day Lakeview view can still be explored on the map.

title: Alba joins Cooksville
summary: The completed Alba tower appeared in the existing city. Harbourwalk and Voya also received more detailed shapes.

details.heading: Following the buildings
details.text: I added Alba in Cooksville. At Voya I refined the curved podium, and at Harbourwalk I revised the model against the developer’s references. The same day brought named project search and the approved massing for 30 Eglinton West.

illustration.alt: The Voya towers in the Downtown model
illustration.caption: The Voya towers in the Downtown model in the November 20 edition. Model by Daniel Sultan.

share.alt: The Voya towers in the Downtown model

title: A second look at the skyline
summary: Community feedback led to corrections at Absolute World and Exchange, and a new set of portrait views.

details.heading: What changed in the model
details.text: I restored missing curves on the south Absolute World tower and revised the top of Exchange’s EX3 against the architect’s published design. I then reframed the portrait series with a softer grey palette.

title: A recognisable preview when you share the site
summary: Shared links began showing the project’s name in their previews.

details.heading: Sharing a view
details.text: I changed the title that appears when a page link is shared, so a reader can recognise Future Mississauga before opening it.

title: Bridges that meet their roads
summary: I corrected bridge elevations and gave the city viewer separate controls for moving and rotating.

details.heading: At river crossings
details.text: I checked how road decks approached bridges in the terrain. The same release added keyboard controls, pointer-centred zoom and a more dependable picture viewer.

title: Checking the city model against its sources
summary: The first documented review compared the city model with municipal records and development plans.

details.heading: The starting point
details.text: City building surveys cover different years. I reviewed the inherited geometry against newer planning information and recorded where a building or route was approximate.
